title: Microinteraction price lab: tiny-query unit economics
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab for thinking through a pricing construct for micro-interactions (single UI actions: short prompt -> short reply, often < 100 tokens). Trying to balance frictionless PLG growth with preventing abuse and keeping unit economics sane for very high volume low-touch UIs (autocomplete, search-suggestions, intent-classifiers).

Context / why this matters:
- We see increasing use of tiny queries (e.g., code completions, snippet lookups, chat comps inside apps). These are high QPS, usually low tokens, but aggregate cost can blow up.
- Existing per-token pricing is fine for mid/large prompts, but awkward for micro UX where product teams want simple per-action pricing or credit friction.
- Goal: 1) Make it easy for product teams to reason about costs, 2) give a low-commit free tier for exploration, 3) keep marginal unit costs covered + ops overhead.

Basic assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Target model for tiny actions: small 7B or distilled model. Effective cost to Redwood (infra + amortized infra overhead): assume $0.00002 per token served (model/runtime cost only). TODO: validate with infra for 4x concurrency variance.
- Average microinteraction tokens: input 25 tokens, output 15 tokens => 40 tokens total per action (this is a working assumption; create sample telemetry bucket).
- Per-action raw compute cost = 40 * 0.00002 = $0.0008 (80 microcents?) Wait math check: 40*0.00002 = 0.0008 = 0.08 cents. So $0.0008 dollars = 0.08¢.
- Add margin + infra overhead (control plane, telemetry, kernel selection, small storage) => x2.5 multiplier => unit cost to us ~ $0.002 per microinteraction.
- Price to customer should cover margin + platform value. Target gross margin 60% => price ~ $0.005 per microinteraction (0.5 cents).

Quick pricing frames to test:
1) Per-interaction plan (simple):
   - Free: 500 microinteractions / month
   - Hobby: $9/mo = 2,000 interactions (~$0.0045 per)
   - Pro: $99/mo = 30,000 interactions (~$0.0033 per)
   - Scale: $499/mo = 200,000 interactions (~$0.0025 per)
   Intent: anchor pricing to unit cost drop with larger committed bundles.

2) Credit-bucket model (blended):
   - 1 credit ~= 1 microinteraction for base model. Sell credits in packs (e.g., 10k credits = $49 -> $0.0049 each)
   - Benefits: aligns with existing credit UX, easy stacking with other token bundles.

3) Hybrid: free per-day limit + per-1000 interactions overage price.

Observations / tradeoffs:
- Per-action simplicity is great for product teams, but creates arbitrage if some apps batch many microinteractions server-side or cache heavily. Need anti-abuse (rate limits, dedupe credits during short windows).
- Caching & client-side aggregation can reduce cost; we should bake signals for "cache-hit" reconciliation so customers don't pay for trivial hits.
- For very high QPS customers (platforms/marketplaces), provide reserved-rate discounts (Dedicated) + private model variants.

Rough revenue math (toy):
- If 1000 customers at Pro ($99/mo): ARR = 1000*99*12 = $1.188M. Interaction volume = 30k*1000 = 30M interactions/mo -> 360M/yr. Cost at $0.002/unit = $720k -> gross margin ~ 40% (low). Need to adjust price or encourage dedicated/reserved for large volumes.

Operational controls to add:
- Minimum per-request token threshold check (don't charge if reply is a zero token no-op)
- Time-window dedupe: if identical request from same API key within 2s, only charge once (configurable).
- Optional client-side SDK hooks that pool micro-interactions (nanobatching) and call a single multi-prompt RPC (saves tokens + lower compute).
- Auto-suggested model downgrade: if customer uses micro interactions but doesn't need strict quality, suggest cheaper distilled model via routing policy.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Telemetry: collect token distribution for top 50 micro-interaction customers (median, p50, p90 tokens).
- Validate infra cost per token for smallest models under sustained micro-QPS (spot instances vs reserved).
- Experiment: 30-day pilot for 10 customers with per-interaction pricing at $0.003 to measure elasticity.
- UX: how to show credits per-action in console without noise? token-level breakout vs per-action count?
- Abuse: how will bots exploit free tier? Need adaptive throttling and CAPTCHA patterns for suspicious keys.

Implementation sketch (engineering notes):
- Billing pipeline: treat microinteraction as a distinct metered unit. Enrich logs with action_type, tokens, cache_hit=true/false. Post-process to create invoice lines with bucket aggregation.
- Console: show "microinteraction balance" + per-route cost insights.
- Dev ergonomics: SDKs return a charge-estimate header for each call so apps can surface incremental cost.

Next steps (short):
- Pull sample of 30k micro-interaction calls across product teams (frontend autocomp, search-suggest, chat quick replies) -> compute distribution. Owner: Rafael. Deadline: 2 weeks.
- Confirm infra per-token cost for candidate model family with infra (SRE). Owner: Maya. Deadline: 1 week.
- Draft simple pricing page copy + FAQs for microinteraction plan (PLG funnel). Owner: Asha (me). Deadline: 3 weeks.

Notes to self: keep options simple for initial launch. Favor credit bundles if we want to reuse existing billing plumbing. Consider dedicated/reserved upsell early for customers who exceed ~100k microinteractions/mo.

Random brainstorm seeds (store these):
- \"micro-burst\" credits that replenish per hour (good for live collaboration apps).
- Meter per \"UI session\" (e.g., 10 actions per session free, then charge).
- Aggregate compression: allow customers to register a list of canonical prompts to be cached and only charge once per canonical entry.

End of scratchpad.
